new.n: R. C. Bennett's $40,000 in coin rolls, Eagle River (found)
new.pl: His 2,000-acre farm near Eagle River; farm not placed (pin on Eagle River)
new.st: Retired electrical-supply man R. C. Bennett, sure paper money would be worthless after the war, buried hundreds of rolls of nickels, dimes and quarters in tin boxes in the basement fruit closet of his farm home from 1936. A note found at his death sent his wife to dig, and two trucks hauled nearly $40,000 in tarnished coin to the First National Bank of Eagle River.
src: United Press, Eagle River, 6 June (1940s; year pending), 'Bank Clerks Count $40,000 in Coins Dug From Cellar' (Neb's clipping)
pinev: His 2,000-acre farm near Eagle River; farm not placed (pin on Eagle River)
new.tovw: Lead grade F (treasure thread): recovered by the family

new.n: Forty casks of beer under the old Henderson brewery (found)
new.pl: Old brewery hillside cellar, Henderson; brewery site not yet pinned exactly
new.st: Brewer Jacob (or Joseph) Ritter stored forty barrels of beer in a cellar dug 30 ft into a hillside about the 1860s; the tunnel caved in. After the brewery was razed, owner Charles Ney let four young men sink a shaft (AP, 14 May, 1920s). By 7 Nov the casks were up and in litigation: the county attorney called them wet contraband, and an heir in St Paul claimed a share.
src: AP, Henderson, 14 May (1920s), 'Search for Beer' (Neb's clipping)
'Finds Beer 60 Years Old', Henderson, 7 Nov (Neb's clipping)
'Heir Asks Share in 40 Casks of Beer' (Neb's clipping)

new.n: Rechenberg's jar of mildewed bills, Dodd Road farm (found 1924)
new.pl: His late father's farm on Dodd Road at the old St Paul limits; farm not placed
new.st: Herman Rechenberg spent four years spading his late father's farm. In January 1924, digging cellar dirt for his chickens, he struck a glass jar holding about $1,300 in mildewed bills, which he banked at the Produce Exchange Bank, St Paul.

new.n: Pierre Pauquette's twenty kegs of gold, Portage (legend)
new.pl: Pauquette's old land at Portage, later taken for a highway; house site not placed
new.st: Fur trader Pierre Pauquette, the 'Wisconsin giant', was killed at Portage in 1836. Rumour held he left twenty kegs of gold buried on his property. Writer Robert E. Gard said that when the highway department took Pauquette's old land and was about to raze the house, he and others dug: 'All we found was a still, and a cache of hickory nuts left by a squirrel.'
new.t: Legend only; Gard's own dig found nothing. Pauquette and the 1836 killing are documented; the kegs are not. Look-only.
src: Kenosha News, Elaine Edwards column on a Robert E. Gard talk (c. 1960s-70s; date pending; Neb's clipping)
pinev: Pauquette's old land at Portage, later taken for a highway; house site not placed
new.tovw: Lead grade D (treasure thread): legend; one dig found nothing

new.n: Money buried above the dam, Niles (French and Indian war legend)
new.pl: 'Just above the dam in this city', St Joseph River, Niles
new.st: Answering the Chicago Chronicle's Bertrand story in December 1898, the Niles Daily Star said no one in Niles had heard of it, but that locals did tell of a large sum buried 'just above the dam in this city' in the French and Indian war.
new.t: One-line local aside; no amount, no finder. Urban riverbank: look-only.

set.st: French trader Joseph Bertrand, founder of Bertrand (4 mi S of Niles), sold land and buried "a full bushel of gold and silver coins" from fear of robbers, then forgot the spot; he believed it was under an apple tree in his orchard. Hundreds searched; "every foot of the orchard" was dug by 1898-99. Pin is between his 1873 house lot and estate, not the spot itself. The earliest wire print found is the Green Bay Press-Gazette of 12 Dec 1898; the wire then ran in Indiana, Ohio, Illinois and New Jersey from 15 Dec, and the first Michigan print found is 28 Dec 1898. The Niles Daily Star (5 Dec 1898) doubted it: the tale came from the Sunday Chicago Chronicle (about 4 Dec 1898) and no one locally had heard of it, though locals did tell of money buried above the Niles dam in the French and Indian war (own pin).
src: Niles Daily Star 5 Dec 1898 p3 (newspapers.com 1020495798, PC (a); re-read and confirmed)
Green Bay Press-Gazette, 12 Dec 1898, p. 10 (Newspapers.com 187615897): earliest print found; ran in IN/OH/IL/NJ from 15 Dec
Livingston County Daily Press and Argus, 28 Dec 1898, p. 7 (Newspapers.com 453547931): first Michigan print found
Bay City Sunday Times, 17 Aug 1902, p. 5, 'Found a Dead Hermit' (Newspapers.com 1183758149); same wire Port Huron 16 Aug p. 8, Kalamazoo 19 Aug p. 6
tw-mi-higgins-lake-flynn-island-hermit-c.st: Israel Porter Pritchard, a former blacksmith and sailor, lived 20-odd years on the island as a county charge; a Bay City sailing party found him dead in his dug-out in Aug 1902.
tw-mi-higgins-lake-flynn-island-hermit-c.t: He died a pauper, which argues against the cache.
